page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g5ne.4xlarge is a General Purpose cloud server provisioned on a KVM hypervisor. It is equipped with an Intel Xeon 8163 x86_64 CPU running at 2.5 GHz, providing 16 dedicated vCPUs derived from 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core. Hardware characteristics include 33 MB of L3 cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache per core, and support for AVX, AVX-512F, AES, FMA, BMI2, and ADX instruction set extensions. The instance is paired with 64.0 GB of memory (4.0 GB per vCPU) and a baseline network interface delivering 7 Gbps bandwidth. This server configuration does not include local disk storage or GPU accelerators.

Benchmark evaluations reveal average multi-core compute capability alongside lower single-core efficiency. Single-core stress-ng tests (1106.79) and single-core Geekbench scores (949.0) fall within the bottom 25% of evaluated cloud hardware, accompanied by lower single-threaded compression performance. Multi-threaded processing scales to average baseline tiers, achieving a Passmark CPU score of 12950.69 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 5846.0. Potentially uncached large block memory throughput reaches 69.78 GB/sec for reads and 51.98 GB/sec for writes.

The primary operational tradeoff of the ecs.g5ne.4xlarge is its limited single-thread throughput, which degrades performance on single-threaded execution paths and medium-sized language model generation (8.62 tokens/sec). However, its standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio provides balanced resource allocation for multi-threaded workloads, including static web serving (7.75 GB/sec), in-memory caching like Redis SET operations (11.72 million ops/sec), database operations, and software compilation.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g5ne.4xlarge is a general-purpose instance featuring an 8-core, 16-vCPU Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz with 64.0 GB of RAM. Running on KVM virtualization with an x86_64 architecture, it incorporates AVX-512F and AES instructions alongside 33 MB of L3 cache and a 7 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance includes no local NVMe storage or dedicated GPUs. Benchmark data highlights average multi-threaded execution capabilities, including a 12950.69 Passmark CPU score, 11.72 million Redis SET ops/sec, and 7.75 GB/sec static web serving throughput. However, single-core performance ranks in the lower 25th percentile, limiting efficiency for single-threaded or heavy model inference workloads. With a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the ecs.g5ne.4xlarge offers reliable hardware resource density for general purpose workloads, software compilation, database tasks, and web services.
